battery-exam-design-campaign-1.title: Exam-design campaign 1 (battery), 2026-09-24
battery-exam-design-campaign-1.summary: A bounded development campaign that solved 2,604 battery references without a failure, tested the gates against authored faults, replayed the exam loop over nine batch and rotation settings, and verified a frozen comparison rule on 200 private cases. It is public/synthetic DEVELOPMENT research: nothing in it is scientifically, security or production qualified.

campaign_plan.title: What a new exam-design study would answer and need
campaign_plan.purpose: Shown when a brief's conditions fall outside Carbon's tested design, or its family has no exam-design evidence. It relays how Carbon ran its first campaign; it is not a plan Carbon has committed to, a price or a quote.
questions: Training data. How many public training cases does a competent model need before more data stops paying for itself?
Screening cases. How many cases must a screening batch hold for a ranking to be stable enough to act on?
Rotation. After how many scored submissions should a screening batch be replaced, so that scores cannot be steered by repeated probing?
Screening validity. Does a model that screens well also do better on fresh cases it has never been scored on?
Reconstruction variability. How much does retraining the same recipe (other seeds; the same seed again) move scores, and does that flip decisions?
Cost. What do a reference case, a screening pass and a finalist comparison actually cost on the declared hardware?
Gates. Do the published gates reject the failures that matter, and only those, without failing correct predictions of unsafe conditions?
